home.heroStatement: Edge COMM-TECH is an integrated technology and systems integration partner, building the infrastructure Ethiopian enterprises depend on and staying with it afterwards.

method.title: Assess
method.body: We start by measuring what you have — load, traffic, utilisation, and risk — because a design built on assumptions is a design that fails commissioning.

method.title: Design
method.body: Documented high-level and low-level designs, issued for your review before anything is ordered. If you cannot review the design, you cannot hold anyone to it.

method.title: Deliver
method.body: Certified engineers, agreed change windows, and a commissioning test that proves the build matches the design before we ask for sign-off.

method.title: Support
method.body: Monitoring, maintenance, and knowledge transfer under a written SLA. The contract that builds it is the contract that keeps it running.

home.sectorsIntro: Built for sectors where downtime is not an option

company.intro: Edge Communication Technologies is an integrated technology solutions and systems integration partner based in Addis Ababa. We design, build, and support the infrastructure that enterprises, financial institutions, and public bodies run on.
company.commitment: We work across the full lifecycle rather than at a single point in it: assessing what an organization has, designing what it needs, commissioning the result, and supporting it afterwards. That continuity is deliberate — most of the failures we are called in to fix originate in a handover where nobody owned what came next.

values.title: Commission, do not just install
values.body: A system is delivered when it has been tested against its design and the results are documented — not when the equipment is racked and the invoice is raised.

values.title: Write it down
values.body: As-built drawings, cable schedules, configuration backups, and runbooks are part of the deliverable. A system that only one person can operate is a liability we refuse to hand over.

values.title: One team from design to support
values.body: The people who designed a system stay reachable once it is running. Continuity removes the handover gap where most long-running faults are born.

values.title: Transfer the knowledge
values.body: We would rather a client could operate what we built without us. Training and documentation are contractual, not an upsell.

solutions.title: Data Center & Critical Systems
solutions.headline: Build the foundation. Commission it properly.
solutions.summary: The physical and critical infrastructure an IT environment actually runs on — power, cooling, containment, cabling, and physical security — designed to a named tier and handed over commissioned, not just installed.

capabilities.name: Tier-rated facility design
capabilities.valueLine: Concurrent maintainability: any capacity component or distribution path can be serviced without stopping the IT load. Agreed as a design target up front, so nobody discovers the limit during an audit.

capabilities.name: Uninterruptible power supply
capabilities.valueLine: Sized against measured load with defined battery autonomy, so the runtime you were sold is the runtime you get on the day the utility drops.

capabilities.name: Redundant power distribution
capabilities.valueLine: One failure or one planned maintenance window is not an outage. Dual-path distribution from source to rack, verified by test rather than assumed.

capabilities.name: Rack power distribution units
capabilities.valueLine: Metered and switched at outlet level: per-device consumption, remote power cycling, and capacity data you can plan the next rack against.

capabilities.name: Precision cooling and containment
capabilities.valueLine: In-row or perimeter cooling with hot and cold aisle containment, keeping inlet temperatures inside vendor specification so warranties stay intact.

capabilities.name: Power usage effectiveness monitoring
capabilities.valueLine: Efficiency measured continuously rather than claimed once, which turns power spend into something you can actually reduce.

capabilities.name: Data center infrastructure management
capabilities.valueLine: Live capacity, environment, and asset data in one place, so growth decisions come from measurements instead of a spreadsheet nobody trusts.

capabilities.name: Structured cabling systems
capabilities.valueLine: Certified, labelled, and documented per link — the difference between a fault found in ten minutes and a fault found in a day.

capabilities.name: Physical access control and surveillance
capabilities.valueLine: Door control, video, and audit trails designed into the room rather than added after an auditor asks who entered it.

capabilities.name: Early smoke detection and suppression
capabilities.valueLine: Aspirating detection catches an event before flame, and clean-agent suppression protects equipment instead of destroying it.

capabilities.name: Generator and automatic transfer
capabilities.valueLine: Standby generation with tested transfer timing, so the gap between utility loss and generator load is covered by the UPS exactly as designed.

scopeOfWork: Site survey, load assessment, and availability-tier workshop with the client
Electrical, mechanical, and structural design with drawings issued for review
Bill of materials with named makes and models, not generic categories
Supply, installation, and containment of power, cooling, racks, and cabling
Physical security: access control, CCTV, detection, and suppression
Commissioning: load bank testing, transfer testing, thermal survey, cable certification
As-built documentation, labelling schedule, and handover training
deliverables: Cable schedule with certification results per link

solutions.title: Cybersecurity & Digital Resilience
solutions.headline: Prevent, detect, respond, recover.
solutions.summary: Security across identity, endpoint, network, application, and data — with the operations capability to run it. A firewall on a quote is a product; a defended organization is an operating discipline.

capabilities.name: Security operations center
capabilities.valueLine: Monitoring with named analysts, defined shifts, and agreed escalation — built around the use cases that matter to your organization rather than a vendor's default rule pack.

capabilities.name: Security information and event management
capabilities.valueLine: Correlated logging across network, endpoint, and identity, so an incident is reconstructable afterwards. That reconstruction is what regulators and insurers ask for.

capabilities.name: Security orchestration and automated response
capabilities.valueLine: Playbooks that isolate a host or disable an account in seconds, so analyst time goes to judgement rather than repetitive containment steps.

capabilities.name: Endpoint and extended detection and response
capabilities.valueLine: Behavioural detection and remote containment on the device itself, including laptops that are not on your network today.

capabilities.name: Network access control
capabilities.valueLine: 802.1X posture and identity checks at the port, so an unmanaged device plugged into a meeting room reaches nothing it should not.

capabilities.name: Next-generation firewall
capabilities.valueLine: Application-aware policy between segments and at the edge, with inspection that still works when the traffic is encrypted.

capabilities.name: Identity and access management
capabilities.valueLine: Joiners, movers, and leavers handled as a process, so access ends when employment does — the finding that appears in almost every first audit.

capabilities.name: Privileged access management
capabilities.valueLine: Administrative credentials checked out, time-bound, and session-recorded, so the accounts that can change everything are the accounts you can prove nobody misused.

capabilities.name: Multi-factor authentication
capabilities.valueLine: The single highest-return control available on remote and privileged access, deployed without making daily work unusable.

capabilities.name: Hardware security module
capabilities.valueLine: Cryptographic keys generated and held in tamper-resistant hardware, never in application memory — a requirement for core banking, PKI, and payment workloads.

capabilities.name: Data loss prevention
capabilities.valueLine: Policy on where regulated data may travel, covering the email and upload paths that perimeter controls never inspect.

capabilities.name: Web application firewall
capabilities.valueLine: Protection for the public services you cannot patch on demand, including the ones a third party built and no longer supports.

capabilities.name: Zero trust network access
capabilities.valueLine: Access granted per application and per identity rather than per network location, which is what makes branch and remote work defensible.

capabilities.name: Backup immutability and disaster recovery
capabilities.valueLine: Immutable copies plus a restore that has actually been rehearsed, against recovery targets the business has signed rather than inherited from a default setting.

capabilities.name: Vulnerability management and testing
capabilities.valueLine: Scanning and penetration testing on a cycle, with remediation tracked to closure instead of filed as a report.

scopeOfWork: Current-state assessment against a named framework (ISO 27001, PCI DSS, or NIST CSF)
Risk and gap analysis with findings ranked by exploitability, not by tool severity
Architecture: segmentation model, identity model, and logging design
Implementation of controls with change windows agreed against business hours
SOC build: use cases, correlation rules, playbooks, escalation matrix
Tabletop exercise and a tested restore before sign-off
Ongoing monitoring, tuning, and periodic re-testing
deliverables: Assessment report with ranked, costed remediation
SIEM use-case catalogue and SOAR playbooks
Incident response plan with named owners
Tested restore evidence against agreed RTO/RPO
Audit evidence pack mapped to your framework

solutions.title: Enterprise Network & Connectivity
solutions.headline: Connect the organization. Keep it converged.
solutions.summary: Campus, branch, wireless, and wide-area connectivity designed as one system — including the voice and collaboration traffic that shares it — and instrumented so problems are found rather than reported.

capabilities.name: Campus and data center switching
capabilities.valueLine: Access, distribution, and core designed with deliberate redundancy, so a single switch failure is a degraded path rather than a dark floor.

capabilities.name: High-density wireless
capabilities.valueLine: Predictive survey against the real building, then post-install validation. Designed for client density and airtime, not for coverage bars on one laptop.

capabilities.name: Software-defined wide area network
capabilities.valueLine: Application-aware path selection across ordinary circuits, with failover measured in seconds and branch policy managed centrally.

capabilities.name: Dynamic routing
capabilities.valueLine: Routing designed for the paths you actually have, including multi-homed internet, so convergence behaviour is known before an outage tests it.

capabilities.name: Gateway redundancy
capabilities.valueLine: No single default gateway to lose. Users keep working through a device failure without raising a support call.

capabilities.name: Network segmentation
capabilities.valueLine: Segments that follow the security model rather than the order things were installed, which is what makes containment possible later.

capabilities.name: Unified communications
capabilities.valueLine: Voice, presence, chat, and conferencing on one platform, with quality of service designed in rather than diagnosed after complaints.

capabilities.name: Application delivery and load balancing
capabilities.valueLine: Published services stay available through a node failure or a maintenance window, and TLS terminates somewhere you control.

capabilities.name: Carrier interconnect
capabilities.valueLine: Provider circuits integrated and managed end to end, so a branch fault has one owner instead of a conversation between vendors.

capabilities.name: Traffic visibility and monitoring
capabilities.valueLine: Who is using what, and when. Turns 'the network is slow' from an argument into a measurement.

scopeOfWork: Discovery of the existing estate, including the parts that are undocumented
Predictive wireless survey and capacity modelling against the real floor plan
High-level and low-level design issued for client review
Staged migration plan with rollback defined for every cutover
Installation, configuration, and cutover inside agreed change windows
Post-install wireless validation survey and performance baseline
Monitoring, configuration backup, and knowledge transfer
deliverables: HLD and LLD documents with addressing and VLAN plan
Predictive and post-install wireless survey reports
Configuration backups and a device inventory

solutions.title: Compute, Cloud & Data Platforms
solutions.headline: Run the workload. Plan the growth.
solutions.summary: Servers, storage, virtualization, and hybrid cloud sized for how the business actually runs — with backup and recovery treated as part of the platform rather than an afterthought.

capabilities.name: Hyperconverged infrastructure
capabilities.valueLine: Compute, storage, and virtualization in one scalable unit — predictable growth increments and one support relationship instead of three.

capabilities.name: Disaggregated hyperconverged infrastructure
capabilities.valueLine: Scale compute and storage independently, so a database that outgrows its capacity does not force you to buy CPU you do not need.

capabilities.name: Enterprise storage
capabilities.valueLine: All-flash and hybrid tiers sized against measured I/O, with replication designed in rather than added when the second site appears.

capabilities.name: Server virtualization
capabilities.valueLine: Consolidation sized on real CPU ready time and memory pressure, which is what keeps performance predictable at high utilisation.

capabilities.name: Private and hybrid cloud
capabilities.valueLine: A deliberate split between local and cloud workloads, with identity and networking bridged — designed before migration rather than discovered on the first invoice.

capabilities.name: Container platforms
capabilities.valueLine: Orchestration introduced when the application team can operate it, with registry, ingress, and persistent storage solved rather than assumed.

capabilities.name: Backup, replication and recovery
capabilities.valueLine: Immutable copies, offsite replication, and a rehearsed restore measured against targets the business has actually signed.

capabilities.name: Database platforms
capabilities.valueLine: Licensing, high availability, and performance designed together, because the cheapest database licence is often the most expensive infrastructure.

capabilities.name: Business intelligence and reporting
capabilities.valueLine: A reporting layer that reads from a modelled warehouse rather than from production, so analysts stop slowing down the system they are measuring.

scopeOfWork: Workload assessment: measured CPU, memory, I/O, and growth trend
Platform selection with a written rationale for HCI, dHCI, or three-tier
Sizing, licensing model, and five-year growth path
Migration design with rollback and an agreed maintenance window
Implementation, migration, and performance validation
Backup and disaster recovery build, plus a proven restore
Capacity reporting and operational handover
deliverables: Backup and DR design with tested restore evidence

solutions.title: Business Applications & Transformation
solutions.headline: Change how the work is done, not just what runs it.
solutions.summary: Enterprise applications, integration, and process automation aligned to how people actually work — measured by what happens after go-live rather than by the size of the software catalogue.

capabilities.name: Enterprise resource planning
capabilities.valueLine: Finance, procurement, inventory, and HR on one record, implemented against your chart of accounts and approval rules rather than a demo dataset.

capabilities.name: Customer relationship management
capabilities.valueLine: A pipeline the sales team actually updates, because it reflects how they sell instead of how the software assumed they would.

capabilities.name: Enterprise content and document management
capabilities.valueLine: Version control, retention policy, and audit trail on documents — usually a regulatory requirement before it is a convenience.

capabilities.name: Business process management
capabilities.valueLine: Processes mapped as they actually run, including the workarounds, then automated. Automating a broken process only makes it faster.

capabilities.name: Systems integration
capabilities.valueLine: Data entered once and trusted everywhere — the difference between owning several systems and running one organization.

capabilities.name: Core banking integration
capabilities.valueLine: Channel, switch, and core interfaces built to the message standards your regulator and partners already use.

capabilities.name: Custom application development
capabilities.valueLine: Built where nothing off the shelf fits, with source, documentation, and handover, so you are not locked to the people who wrote it.

capabilities.name: Adoption and change management
capabilities.valueLine: Training, floorwalking, and a defined support path after go-live, measured by how much of the process is still in the system after ninety days.

scopeOfWork: Process discovery workshops with the people who do the work
Requirements and fit-gap analysis against candidate platforms
Solution and integration architecture
Configuration, development, and data migration
User acceptance testing with real transactions
Training, go-live support, and floorwalking
Post-go-live review at thirty and ninety days
deliverables: Process maps, current and target state
Migrated and reconciled data with sign-off

solutions.title: Professional Services
solutions.headline: From assessment to knowledge transfer.
solutions.summary: Certified engineers across the full lifecycle — assessment, design, implementation, managed operations, and support — so an investment stays aligned long after the installation team leaves.

capabilities.name: Infrastructure assessment and audit
capabilities.valueLine: An independent view of what you have, what it costs to run, and where risk concentrates — written to be readable by finance as well as by IT.

capabilities.name: Architecture and detailed design
capabilities.valueLine: Designs issued as reviewable documents you could hand to any integrator, which is what makes a build auditable later.

capabilities.name: Implementation and commissioning
capabilities.valueLine: Certified engineers, agreed change windows, and a commissioning test that proves the system meets the design before sign-off.

capabilities.name: Network and security operations
capabilities.valueLine: Monitoring, patching, backup verification, and vendor case management run as a service, so your team is not the alerting system.

capabilities.name: Service level agreements
capabilities.valueLine: Response and restoration targets in writing, with reporting against them — the difference between support and best effort.

capabilities.name: Managed IT helpdesk
capabilities.valueLine: Ticketed first- and second-line support, remote and on site, with the history to spot the recurring fault nobody had time to trace.

capabilities.name: Staff augmentation and mentoring
capabilities.valueLine: Certified engineers embedded with your team, transferring capability rather than protecting it.

capabilities.name: Lifecycle and warranty management
capabilities.valueLine: Tracked end-of-life and support dates, so refresh is a budgeted plan instead of an emergency after a failure.

scopeOfWork: Discovery and independent assessment of the current estate
Design documentation issued for client review and sign-off
Implementation, migration, and commissioning
Monitoring onboarding and runbook development
Managed service transition with agreed SLA targets
Periodic service review and capacity reporting
Documentation, handover, and structured knowledge transfer
deliverables: Assessment report with prioritised, costed findings

sectors.title: Government & Health
sectors.line: Where uptime is a public duty — ministries, agencies, universities, and health systems.

pressures.title: Procurement scrutiny
pressures.detail: Specifications, bills of material, and commissioning evidence have to withstand review by an audit body months after handover. Undocumented work becomes a finding.

pressures.title: Continuity of public service
pressures.detail: A failed system is not an internal inconvenience. Maintenance windows are narrow, and concurrent maintainability stops being a nice-to-have.

pressures.title: Patient and citizen data
pressures.detail: Access control, retention, and audit trail on records — with the ability to answer who accessed a file and when.

pressures.title: Skills retention
pressures.detail: Public institutions lose engineers to the private sector. Systems must be documented and operable by the next person, and knowledge transfer needs to be contractual.

sectors.title: Banking & Finance
sectors.line: Core rooms, identity, and networks that auditors can walk through end to end.

pressures.title: Regulatory examination
pressures.detail: Controls must produce evidence on demand. Logging, access review, and change records are examined rather than described.

pressures.title: Key custody
pressures.detail: Cryptographic material held in HSMs with documented ceremony and dual control. Software key storage does not pass review.

pressures.title: Recovery targets
pressures.detail: RTO and RPO agreed at board level, with tested restores and retained evidence — not a backup job that reports success.

pressures.title: Branch estate
pressures.detail: Dozens or hundreds of sites on variable connectivity, each needing consistent policy, predictable failover, and central management.

sectors.title: Telecommunications
sectors.line: Carrier-grade operations for the providers other organizations depend on.

pressures.title: Downstream blast radius
pressures.detail: An outage affects every customer at once, so change control, rollback, and staged deployment are engineering requirements rather than governance overhead.

pressures.title: Continuous capacity growth
pressures.detail: Traffic growth is measured monthly. Platforms are chosen on how they scale, not on what they cost to start.

pressures.title: Operational density
pressures.detail: Thousands of devices make manual configuration untenable. Automation and compliance checking are the only way estates stay consistent.

pressures.title: Facility density
pressures.detail: High power-density racks put real pressure on cooling design, containment, and PUE.

sectors.title: International organizations
sectors.line: Missions and programmes that need global standards delivered on local ground.

pressures.title: Headquarters compliance
pressures.detail: Security baselines and approved vendor lists are set centrally. Local delivery must meet them and evidence it in the required format.

pressures.title: Field conditions
pressures.detail: Unreliable power and connectivity at programme sites, requiring resilient links, local resilience, and graceful degradation.

pressures.title: Staff rotation
pressures.detail: Administrators change every posting cycle, so documentation and handover quality determine whether the system survives.

pressures.title: Procurement and audit
pressures.detail: Donor-funded spend is audited closely. Traceable specification, quotation, and delivery records are part of the deliverable.
